prompt: What does the tag `latest` guarantee about an image?

choices.text: That it is the newest build in the registry
choices.why: It is wherever the last push that named it left it.

choices.text: That it passed the publisher's tests
choices.why: No tag says anything about tests.

choices.text: Nothing; it is the tag used when none is given
choices.why: Right. It could be the oldest build there is.

choices.text: That it is the most recent stable release
choices.why: Publishers often do point it there, by choice; nothing enforces it.

prompt: After the 1.1.0 push, `docker ps` showed `web-a` with a bare id in the `IMAGE` column. Why?

choices.text: The container crashed and lost its image
choices.why: Its log showed it listening; it was running.

choices.text: `docker ps` abbreviates long names
choices.why: It showed the full name for `web-b`.

choices.text: Containers started from a registry show ids
choices.why: `web-b` came from the same registry and showed the name.

choices.text: The name it started from now belongs to another image
choices.why: Right: the tag moved to 1.1.0, so only the id still names `web-a`'s image.

prompt: A server pulled `shelf:latest` in March. In June, after several pushes, it runs `docker run shelf:latest` again. What does it run?

choices.text: March's build, the one it already has
choices.why: Right, until somebody pulls again or runs with `--pull always`.

choices.text: June's build, because `docker run` always asks the registry
choices.why: By default it pulls only when the name is missing on the machine.

choices.text: Nothing; Docker refuses a stale tag
choices.why: Docker has no idea the tag is stale.

choices.text: A random choice between the two builds
choices.why: There is nothing random: the local name points at one image.

prompt: Which of these are costs of deploying `latest`? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Rolling back needs a name `latest` cannot give
choices.why: Yes: it only names what is there now.

choices.text: Nobody can say which version answered a bug report
choices.why: Yes: the tag pointed somewhere else that day.

choices.text: `FROM` with `latest` gets new compilers unasked
choices.why: Yes, which hadolint's `DL3007` refuses.

choices.text: Images tagged `latest` are larger
choices.why: A tag is a name; it adds nothing to the image.

prompt: `shelf` 1.2.4 is released. Under the lesson's scheme, which tags go on the new build?
hint: Which tags follow the newest build, and which name one?

choices.why: Then `1.2` and `1` would still offer the build without the fix.
Right, plus the new commit's `sha-` tag when there is one.
`1.2.3` names one release, and must keep naming it.

choices.text: `latest` only, so everyone gets the fix
choices.why: Nothing in the scheme reads `latest`; people asking for `1.2` would miss it.

prompt: Why are the `LABEL` and its `ARG` lines in the final stage of Ana's Dockerfile, not the build stage?

choices.text: BuildKit refuses `LABEL` in a stage based on the official `golang` image
choices.why: Any stage accepts `LABEL`; it would just stay in that stage.

choices.text: Labels must come after `USER`
choices.why: Order is free; Ana's come before `COPY`.

choices.text: Only the final stage's labels and arguments reach the image
choices.why: Right: the build stage leaves only `/out/shelf`, and an `ARG` is visible only in its own stage.

choices.text: BuildKit runs the final stage first
choices.why: It runs what the final stage needs; the order is not the reason.

prompt: An image is copied to a second registry under a new name. What still says which commit it came from?
hint: Which of the two lives inside the image?

choices.text: Its old `sha-12d9616` tag
choices.why: Tags belong to a registry, and the copy did not take them.

choices.text: Nothing; that information is lost
choices.why: It is written inside the image.

choices.text: The registry's upload log
choices.why: That is in the first registry, if anywhere.

choices.text: Its `org.opencontainers.image.revision` label
choices.why: Right: labels live in the image and travel with it.

prompt: Ana pushed a different build as `1.2.3`, and `registry:3` accepted it. What would have refused it?
hint: The lesson named a setting in two hosted registries.

choices.text: Making the tag immutable in a registry that supports it
choices.why: Right, though a digest is still the only reference the bytes guarantee.

choices.text: Nothing: no registry can refuse a push to an existing tag
choices.why: ECR and Artifact Registry both can.

choices.text: Logging in first
choices.why: Logging in only proves who pushed it.

choices.text: Adding an `org.opencontainers.image.version` label
choices.why: A label describes an image; it does not protect a tag.

prompt: Lesson 15's and lesson 16's builds of `shelf` 1.0.0, from the same source, had different ids. How many distinct ids is that?
Match each tag on `shelf` to what it names.
hint: Two name one build; two follow the newest.

pairs.right: The commit it was built from

right_distractors: The newest build pushed with no tag

prompt: Ana wrote `golang:1.25@sha256:6993…`, keeping the tag. What does Docker use to choose the image?
hint: The build log said what it loaded.

choices.text: The tag, and the digest is a comment
choices.why: The digest decides; the build resolved `@sha256:` itself.

choices.text: The digest; the tag is for readers
choices.why: Right: a person sees Go 1.25, and Docker fetches those bytes.

choices.text: Whichever of the two was pushed more recently
choices.why: A digest is not newer or older; it names one image.

choices.text: Both, and the build fails unless they agree
choices.why: Docker resolves the digest and does not ask the registry where the tag is.

prompt: Pinning the bases by digest has a cost. What is it?

choices.text: Builds become slower, since every digest is checked against the registry
choices.why: Resolving a digest costs no more than resolving a tag.

choices.text: The image grows by the size of the digest
choices.why: The digest is in the Dockerfile, not added to the image.

choices.text: Base image security fixes wait for a changed line
choices.why: Right, which is why a bot proposes the new digest as a pull request.

choices.text: The Dockerfile only builds on Ana's machine
choices.why: Any machine that can reach the registry fetches the same bytes.

prompt: GitHub's built-in bot that opens a pull request with a new base image digest is called ___.
hint: Renovate is the other one named.

prompt: `docker inspect web --format "{{.Config.Image}}"` printed `localhost:5000/shelf@sha256:e836…`. What does that say?
hint: What was the container started from?

choices.text: That the tag `1.3.0` was deleted
choices.why: The tag is still in the registry; it just was not used.

choices.text: That the image has no labels
choices.why: Labels are under `.Config.Labels`; this field is the reference.

choices.text: That the registry rewrote the reference
choices.why: The reference is what Ana typed in `docker run`.

choices.text: That `web` was started by digest
choices.why: Right, so it runs those bytes whatever the tag does.

prompt: Match each need to the reference that serves it.
hint: Who should decide when it changes?

pairs.left: Try an image out by hand, today
Get fixes, but no new features
Run exactly what passed the tests
Find the commit behind a build

prompt: A colleague's deployment file says `image: shelf:1.2.3`. Which change makes it run only what was tested, whatever the registry does?
hint: A tag can be pushed over, as Ana showed.

choices.text: Append `@sha256:` and the digest the tested push printed
choices.why: Right: the tag stays for readers, and the digest decides.

choices.text: Change it to `shelf:1.2`
choices.why: That moves on purpose, with every patch.

choices.text: Add `--pull always` to the start command
choices.why: That fetches whatever the tag points at now, overwrite included.

choices.text: Change it to `shelf:latest` and pin the registry's address
choices.why: A registry cannot be pinned; `latest` moves on every push.
